original_statement:
Request: Origin: exophial exo-011 (2026-07-18), rule 5 (optional tier) of the sourced design; assigned to aspergillus but never filed there (filed 2026-07-22).

THE RULE: an if/elif or match dispatching on == comparisons against string literals, where the string literal set intersects the value set of an Enum defined/imported in the same module → WARN 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'.

WHY: string dispatch is invisible to both mypy exhaustive-match and ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE — it is the opt-out below the opt-out. exophial's FSM history (the two-enum split, status_to_action) shows internal string routing is where states silently multiply.

BOUNDARY OPT-OUT (required by exo-011's design): parsers at serialization boundaries (bus deserialization, handoff YAML status, CLI args) legitimately compare strings BEFORE the typed world begins. Opt-out via a marker comment on the function (e.g. '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse'), mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom.

ACCEPTANCE: fixture with (1) string-literal dispatch shadowing a same-module Enum → WARNED; (2) same function bearing the boundary marker → silent; (3) string dispatch with no corresponding Enum → silent.

DEPENDS ON asp-26e only for the shared enum-subject detection helper, if extracted; otherwise independent.
restatement: This request asks aspergillus to gain a new lint rule, derived from exophial's exo-011 design (rule 5, the optional tier), assigned to aspergillus on 2026-07-18 but only filed on 2026-07-22. The rule targets 'stringly-typed dispatch': an if/elif chain or a match statement that branches by comparing a value with == against string literals, in the specific case where that set of string literals overlaps with the value set of an Enum class that is defined or imported in that same module. This pattern is dangerous because it silently bypasses both mypy's exhaustiveness checking and aspergillus's own ASP-FSM-EXHAUSTIVE check — routing on raw strings instead of on the Enum is exactly how exophial's own FSM history saw states silently multiply (the two-enum split, status_to_action). When the rule finds this pattern, it must emit a WARN-level diagnostic reading exactly 'stringly-typed dispatch; dispatch on the Enum so exhaustiveness checking applies'. The rule must also honor a documented escape hatch required by exo-011's design: a function carrying a marker comment such as '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse' — mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom — is understood to be a boundary parser (bus deserialization, handoff YAML status, CLI args) that legitimately compares raw strings before the typed world begins, and must never be warned about even if it otherwise matches the pattern. Conversely, ordinary string-literal dispatch that has no corresponding same-module Enum at all is not the targeted antipattern and must stay silent. Implementation may reuse a shared enum-subject-detection helper from asp-26e if one gets extracted there, but is not required to depend on it.

Opt-out via a marker comment on the function (e.g. '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse'), mirroring aspergillus's existing lint-ignore idiom — fixture: (2) same function bearing the boundary marker → silent
fixture with ... (3) string dispatch with no corresponding Enum → silent

goal: Add a stringly-typed-dispatch lint rule to aspergillus that WARNs when if/elif or match string-literal dispatch shadows a same-module Enum, stays silent on functions marked '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse', and stays silent when no corresponding Enum exists.
acceptance_criteria: Feed the checker a code sample where a function dispatches on string comparisons ('pending', 'done') that match the values of an Enum defined right there in the same file. The checker should report exactly one warning, and its wording should be exactly the required message about stringly-typed dispatch.

Feed the checker the exact same code sample as above, except the function now carries the marker comment '# asp-fsm: boundary-parse' just above the dispatch. The checker should report zero warnings for this file.

Feed the checker a code sample that dispatches on the same string literals ('pending', 'done') but where no Enum exists anywhere in the file. The checker should report zero warnings, since there is no Enum being shadowed.
